territorial_scope.description: Applies to controllers and processors established in Uruguay, and to those not established there where their processing offers goods or services to inhabitants of the Republic, analyses their behaviour, uses means located in the country, or is required by international law or contract.

evidence.quote: Las actividades de tratamiento de datos están relacionadas con la oferta de bienes o servicios dirigidos a habitantes de la República

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Implements Uruguay's personal data protection law (Laws 19.670 and 18.331): extends duties to controllers abroad in listed cases, sets security and breach-notification rules, requires impact assessments and data protection officers for specified entities. Published 21/02/2020.
summary.long: Regulates Articles 37 to 40 of Law 19.670 and Article 12 of Law 18.331 on personal data protection. Articles 1-2 extend Law 18.331, including its database registration duties, to controllers or processors not established in Uruguay where they offer goods or services to inhabitants, analyse inhabitants' behaviour, use means located in the country, or are bound by international law or contract. Article 3 requires technical and organisational security measures and initial containment steps within 24 hours of a security incident. Article 4 requires notice to the Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales within 72 hours of a breach, notice to affected data subjects in clear language where their rights are significantly affected, and a final report. Articles 5-9 require documented, periodically reviewed proactive measures; impact assessments before processing in listed cases (including sensitive data as core business, profiling, vulnerable groups, and large volumes); and privacy by design and by default. Articles 10-15 require a data protection officer for public entities, private entities mainly processing sensitive data, and private entities processing data of more than 35,000 persons; designation must be notified within 90 days. Article 16 empowers the Unidad to set criteria, and its Consejo Ejecutivo to impose sanctions under Law 18.331 Art. 35. Article 17 repeals Articles 7 and 8 of Decree 414/009. Processing already under way that falls within Article 6 must be assessed within one year of publication in the Diario Oficial.

thresholds.variable_text: tratamiento de grandes volúmenes de datos: tratamiento de datos personales de más de 35.000 personas
thresholds.measurement: Not stated in the text: no window or aggregation method is given. The clause defines large-volume processing as any activity processing personal data of more than 35,000 persons.
thresholds.consequence: Private entities that carry out large-volume processing must designate a data protection officer (delegado de protección de datos personales).
thresholds.conditions: Applies to private entities under Art. 10 literal c). Art. 10 literal a) (public and partly state-owned entities) and literal b) (private entities processing sensitive data as their main business) are separate grounds. The Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales may also rule on whether a private entity must have a DPO. Art. 6 literal e) requires an impact assessment for large-volume processing, without restating this number.

evidence.quote: Se considera tratamiento de grandes volúmenes de datos cualquier actividad en la que se realice un tratamiento de datos personales de más de 35.000 personas.
